name: Pentadeca Arginate
summary: A peptide described as an arginine salt of the experimental peptide BPC-157, used for injury healing; it has not been tested in published studies and is not FDA-approved.
what_it_is: Pentadeca arginate (PDA) is the name used for a form of BPC-157 combined with the amino acid arginine. BPC-157 is a lab-made peptide of 15 amino acids (a 'pentadecapeptide') taken from a protein first isolated from human gastric juice. No peer-reviewed study or FDA document about PDA itself was found, so its exact make-up, and whether it acts like other forms of BPC-157, cannot be confirmed; FDA notes that several salts and derivatives are sold under the BPC-157 name.

evidence.why: No studies of PDA itself were found; claims rest on animal research on BPC-157, whose few small human studies FDA judged insufficient.

status_us.label: Not approved; not on any FDA compounding list
status_us.note: No PDA product is approved, and 'pentadeca arginate' is not on FDA's May 2026 compounding nominations list or its Category 2 page; FDA's July 2026 BPC-157 review covered only the free base and acetate forms, so this salt's status is unclear. BPC-157 itself awaits FDA action after an 8-6 advisory vote in favor in July 2026, and WADA bans non-approved substances such as BPC-157 in sport.

benefits.claim: Faster tendon healing and protection of the stomach, intestines and liver in rodent studies of BPC-157, the parent peptide; PDA itself has not been tested
Colon fistulas about 40% smaller than in untreated rats, and closed by day 28, with BPC-157

risks.risk: No human safety data for PDA, and too little for BPC-157 to describe its side effects
Immune reactions, which FDA called a possibly significant risk for BPC-157 that clumping or impurities could make worse
Unknown cancer risk: no studies of BPC-157's cancer-causing potential exist
Uncertain identity: FDA says several salts and derivatives are sold under the BPC-157 name, so a patient may get a different substance than the one prescribed

avoid_if: Current or past cancer (cancer risk has not been studied)
Competitive athletes (WADA bans non-approved substances such as BPC-157)

labs.why: No evidence-based monitoring exists for PDA or BPC-157.

studies.title: FDA Briefing Document for BPC-157-Related Bulk Drug Substances (BPC-157 (free base) and BPC-157 acetate)
studies.people: Published BPC-157 studies, including 5 small human studies; none of PDA
studies.finding: FDA found too little clinical safety information to characterize BPC-157's safety, flagged possible immune reactions and impurities, and said the animal healing results had significant limitations.

notes_for_editor: Status unclear. No peer-reviewed, FDA or other authoritative source describing pentadeca arginate was found; search results were vendor pages, which were not cited. The identity used here (an arginine salt of BPC-157) rests on the product name and the catalog's aliases. FDA's BPC-157 review covered only the free base and acetate and warns that other salts and derivatives are sold under the same name; whether pharmacies may lawfully compound PDA, and whether an FDA decision on BPC-157 would cover it, is unresolved. Re-check after FDA acts on BPC-157 and on the pending HHS interim peptide policy.
